A.explanation: Half the correct frequency, from using $83.5 - 17.1 = 66.4\text{ cm}$ as a full wavelength instead of half a wavelength.

B.explanation: The $66.4\text{ cm}$ separation is $\lambda/2$, giving $\lambda = 1.328\text{ m}$ and $f = 340/1.328 \approx 256\text{ Hz}$.

C.explanation: Too large by a factor of 1.5, from confusing first and second resonance lengths with $\lambda/4$ and $3\lambda/4$ without using their difference correctly.

D.explanation: Double the correct frequency, from using $66.4\text{ cm}$ as $\lambda$ instead of $\lambda/2$ and then doubling again in error.

hints: Notice the two loud positions are at water heights $83.5\text{ cm}$ and $17.1\text{ cm}$ above the bench, so find the change in air-column length as the water is lowered.
Recall that the air column with water at the bottom is closed at one end, so successive resonances (loud sounds) are separated by half a wavelength $\lambda/2$.
Use $v = f\lambda$ with $v = 340\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and your value of $\lambda$ from twice the $66.4\text{ cm}$ separation, remembering to convert cm to m.
walkthrough: The loud sounds are resonances of the air column above the water. The water surface acts as a closed end and the top of the cylinder is open.
The air-column length increases as the water level falls. The increase between the two loud sounds is $83.5 - 17.1 = 66.4\text{ cm} = 0.664\text{ m}$.
For a closed tube, successive stationary-wave resonances occur when the length increases by $\lambda/2$. So $\lambda/2 = 0.664\text{ m}$.
This gives $f \approx 256\text{ Hz}$ with unit $\text{Hz}$ as required. This is option B.
